ellen (eng-runtime): Heads up — I hit a correctness edge with prefix caching yesterday in canary. Short thread to sync on options.

sam (infra): what happened?

ellen (eng-runtime): One of our long-running chat sessions observed repeated hallucinated token continuations after a KV eviction race. Seems like the prefix was evicted mid-request, then a prefetch refilled a stale partial KV and we served it.

jia (ml-ops): ouch. Can you paste a minimal repro trace?

ellen (eng-runtime): Sure — simplified log:
```
REQ id=abc123 prefix=p1 seq=0..1024
CACHE-EVICT shard=3 prefix=p1 at=ts1
PREFETCH start for p1 (from disk) at=ts1+5ms
SERVE token generation used KV-state version v_old (incomplete)
```
The key is the eviction and concurrent prefetch; prefetch returned an intermediate view before the compaction completed.

kevin (platform): do we have versioned KV entries? We should be able to detect and reject partial state by version/tag.

sam (infra): we do keep a `seq`-style generation number for writes, but eviction currently just drops the in-memory block; prefetch pulls blobs from object store which might be partially updated if a write and compaction race.

jia (ml-ops): sounds like two problems: (1) stale/partial state visibility, (2) lack of atomic handover when swapping in a new prefix.

ellen (eng-runtime): Exactly. Proposal A: introduce a single-writer lease per prefix that guarantees only the lease-holder can install a new in-memory version, and readers must check a `stable` bit. If `stable=false` readers wait or fall back.

sam (infra): Lease makes sense for correctness but worries: latency headroom for hot prefixes. If a burst of requests waits on a writer to finish, P99 will spike.

kevin (platform): alternative: soft-handoff with copy-on-write + epoch tags: prefetch computes new blob and atomically bumps a prefix-epoch pointer only after full validation. Readers always compare epoch. If mismatch, they retry once. That avoids serializing reads on the writer.

ellen (eng-runtime): I like epoch tags. But we still need a way to prevent both writer and prefetch from installing two different partial views concurrently (write amplification).

jia (ml-ops): what about combining both: a lightweight lease used only during install/validation (10s ms), but readers do epoch-check and optimistic fast path. So most reads are lock-free; installs are serialized briefly.

sam (infra): implementation detail: per-shard lease coordinator? We have >200 shards, can't do a global lock. Per-prefix ephemeral lock in shard owner is fine. We'll use CAS on the prefix descriptor in the shard metadata.

kevin (platform): also need metrics: `install_duration_ms`, `install_retries`, `reader_epoch_mismatch_count` so we can tune.

ellen (eng-runtime): agree. Another related tradeoff: eviction policy. If we pin very hot prefixes to avoid churn, multilayer fairness suffers — multi-tenant customers could starve each other.

jia (ml-ops): propose eviction watermark + tenant budget: each tenant gets a soft-residency budget. If exceeded, we evict LRU across their prefixes but allow transient bursts. That reduces cross-tenant noisy-neighboring.

sam (infra): plus a global eviction signal from infra when memory pressure crosses 80% to trigger more aggressive reclamation.

kevin (platform): we should document the invariants: (1) readers must never see partially-installed prefix; (2) installs should be idempotent; (3) eviction must not drop a prefix mid-serve unless the prefix is not being referenced (ref-count).

ellen (eng-runtime): ref-counting at runtime is heavy, but we can maintain an `in-flight` counter per prefix (atomic) that prevents final eviction until 0. This handles in-flight requests without global locking.

jia (ml-ops): one more gotcha: prefetch/multi-tenant prewarming. If prefetch threads saturate IO, they can slow down installs for real-time reads. We should prioritize on-path installs over background prefetch.

sam (infra): yep — implement a priority queue for fetch workers: high-prio for installs triggered by reads, low-prio for background prefetch/refresh.

kevin (platform): ok action items: 1) add epoch tags + CAS-based install API, 2) add ephemeral install lease to avoid dual-installs, 3) add in-flight counters to defer eviction, 4) tenant soft-residency budgets + global memory watermark signal, 5) metrics and QA test for eviction race.

ellen (eng-runtime): I'll draft a small follow-up RFC with API sketches. Quick pseudo-API:
```
// returns current epoch; install only succeeds if epoch matches
bool InstallPrefix(prefix, expected_epoch, new_blob, new_epoch)
// reader flow
epoch = ReadEpoch(prefix); state = ReadBlob(prefix); if (ReadEpoch(prefix) != epoch) retry once
```
I'll include the corner-case tests.

jia (ml-ops): include a repro test that asserts no-serving-of-partial by injecting delays and forcing eviction+prefetch races.

sam (infra): I'll prototype the CAS on shard metadata and the priority fetch queue.  ETA 1 week.

kevin (platform): I'll add the metrics and a dashboard.

cache-bot: scheduled test-run "kv-eviction-race" in staging for 1751122900 :robot_face:

ellen (eng-runtime): thanks all. If anyone has objections to the combined approach (epoch + short install lease + in-flight counters), shout here. Otherwise I'll start the RFC tomorrow. :thumbsup:
